podcast.body: As the theme song for David Lynch's "Twin Peaks," this track from Julee Cruise's 1989 album "Floating Into the Night" (with Angelo Badalamenti) epitomizes the dreamy, hazy, and blurry mood characteristic of late 1980s Dreampop, often featuring quiet, breathy female vocals.

podcast.body: This pioneering dream pop song was produced by filmmaker David Lynch. It originated as an instrumental composition titled "Falling," commissioned from songwriter Angelo Badalamenti for Lynch's 1989 TV series "Twin Peaks." After the show became a hit, Julee Cruise recorded the vocal version for her album "Floating into the Night," which then became a significant hit. It reached number one in Australia, number two in Finland and Sweden, number three in Italy and Norway, number seven in the UK, and number eight in Denmark, also becoming a modern rock radio hit in both Canada and the US. Cruise performed the song on Saturday Night Live, and it was used in other movies and TV shows. "Falling" is recognized as a landmark song in the dream pop genre, and in 2012, Britain's NME included it on their list of the 100 best songs of the 90s. As of February 2026, it had over 34 million combined plays (26.6 million on Spotify and 8.5 million on YouTube), earning a one-hit wonder score of 3.55. "Her only real hit was a pioneering dream pop song produced by filmmaker David Lynch."
